Interview Experience - FTE 2024
Neel Shah | Computer Engineering | Batch 2024
Role offered: Software Developer
Compensation Details:

BNY Mellon came to our campus to recruit final-year students for an FTE position as a software developer. There were more than 150 applicants.
Eligibility: 7.5 CGPA Criteria
Branches Allowed: CS, IT, EXTC, Electronics, Electrical, and Mechanical.
About BNY Mellon:
The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation, commonly known as BNY Mellon, is an American investment banking services holding company headquartered in New York City. BNY Mellon was formed from the merger of The Bank of New York and the Mellon Financial Corporation in 2007. It is the world's largest custodian bank and securities services company, with $1.8 trillion in assets under management and $44.3 trillion in assets under custody at the end of 2022.

Round 1 - Online Assessment [120 mins] (10th August 2023)
Online Test conducted on Hackerrank Platform having 4 DSA Questions to be completed within 120 Minutes. The level of the questions was moderate to difficult. There were 1 easy, 2 medium and 1 difficult question.
1. Binary Storage -
You’re given a binary 2D array of size NxM, each row of the matrix had some value x denoting the xth bit of the current number is set. Consider arr[] = {3,2,1} meaning the number would be 1110 which is equivalent to 14, similarly, other N rows would contribute some value you have to sort in descending order of values and return the indices according to row number.
Eg - bitArrays = [[0,2],[2,3],[2,1]]
here, the values in order of descending are [12,6,5] so, we return [1,2,0].
I was able to solve this completely.

2. Merge Sort Counts
An array has n elements. If the array has less than 2 elements, then the array is returned without any changes. If the array has more than two elements, then it is divided into two arrays, left and right. The left array contains the first half elements of the input array while the right array contains the second half of the elements. If n is odd, the left array takes the middle element. Next, the algorithm calls itself first with the left array and then with the right array. After that, the algorithm produces the sorted array, by merging the left and the right arrays into a single sorted array. In this challenge, keep a count for each of the elements in the input array. Initially, all counts are 0. Whenever an integer k from the right array is merged before at least one element from the left array, add 1 to the count. Find the maximum count value after the merge sort algorithm finishes.
Example
arr = [2, 3, 1]
All counters are initialized to 0. First, the mergesort divides the input array into left [2,3] and right = [1]. Next, it runs itself again with the left array. It divides this array into [2] and [3]. Since both are sorted, it merges them, and during the merge 3 is merged after 2 into the sorted order, so nothing is added to the counter. After the merge, the algorithm returns [2,3] to its caller. Next, the initial mergesort call runs itself for the right array [1] but since it has only one element no merging is performed and [1] is returned immediately. Next, the algorithm merges [2,3] with [1]. Since 1 from the right array comes before both elements from the left array during the merge, we add 1 to the counter. After this merge, the algorithm finishes, and the maximum count after the process is 1.
Function Description
Complete the function largestCountValue. The function must return an integer that denotes the maximum count value after the entire merge sort algorithm finishes for the input array arr.

The first step, break the array into left = [1, 2, 3] and right = [4, 5, 10]. Now break left into left' = [1, 2] and right' = [3]. Break left' into left"= [1] and right" = [2]. Perform the merge to get res" = [1, 2]. The element from right" was not inserted before an element of left", so the count remains 0. Merge res" and right' to get res' = [1, 2, 3]. Again, no element of right' was inserted before an element of res", so the count remains 0. The array right uses the same logic to arrive at a count of 0. Finally, merging [1, 2, 3] and [4, 5, 10], no element from the right array is inserted before any element of the left array has been inserted, so the count remains 0.
This was a slight variation of counting inversions problem using Merge Sort.
I was able to pass 4/15 test cases in this question as I made some silly mistakes.

3. Server Investment
A network security administrator must protect networks at a number of locations from cyber-attacks. Initially, the ith network has num_server[i] servers, and money[i] funds allocated for security upgrades. To upgrade a server in the ith network, it costs upgrade[i]. Selling a server adds sell[i] to available funds.
Given the arrays num_servers, money, upgrade, and sell, each with n integers, determine the maximum number of servers that can be upgraded to ensure optimal network security. The result should be an array of n integers, where the ith integer represents the maximum number of upgraded servers for the ith network system.
Given, num servers - [4, 3], money = [8, 9]. sell = [4, 2] and upgrade - [4, 5]
System Description | No. of upgraded servers
1st | A server can be sold at a cost of 4 and upgraded at a cost of 4. If one server is sold, the total amount left is 8+4=12 and 3 servers will be left. Now each server can be upgraded at a cost of 4 for each | 3
2nd | One server can be sold for a cost of 2 amounting to total money of 11 units which can be used to upgrade both of the remaining servers at a cost of 10 units | 2
Hence the answer is [3,2]

4. Team Formation
Given a list of employees where each is assigned a numeric evaluation score, use the selection process below to find the sum of scores of selected employees.
1. The employee with the highest score among the first k employees or the last k employees in the score list is selected.
2. The selected employee is removed from the score list.
3. The process continues to select the next employee until the team size is achieved.
Note:
1. In case multiple employees have the same highest score, the employee with the lowest index is selected.
2. If there are fewer than k employees, the entire list is available for selection.
Example
score = [10, 20, 10, 15, 5, 30, 20]
teamSize=2
k=3
• For the first selection, choose from the first 3 elements: [10, 20, 10] or the last 3 elements: [5, 30, 20]. Score 30 is selected and removed from the list. This makes the score = [10, 20, 10, 15, 5, 20].
• For the second selection, choose from [10, 20, 10] or [15, 5, 20]. Score 20 is selected from the lowest index and removed from the list. This makes the score = [10, 10, 15, 5, 20]. The sum of the selected employees' scores is 30+20=50.
I tried to solve this questions using multiple approaches but the Multiset approach worked but still it passed only 7/15 test cases.

After being not shortlisted for 2 companies consecutively - Deutsche Bank and Oracle, I had a lot of anxiety since this was the last dream company in August and all other companies may be invited by mid september. Inspite of having a strong profile, i was not able to sit for the interviews, But finally I was shortlisted for BNY Mellon!
19 students were shortlisted for the interviews, but later on, 6 more were shortlisted. All the interviews were conducted in person.

Technical Round 1 (45 mins) (17th August 2023)
1. The interviewer was friendly and he made me comfortable and asked me to sit. He then started with a very famous question “Please introduce yourself?” (Be prepared with your introduction beforehand only)
2. Later he told me let's test your coding skills and gave me 3 dsa questions. (We need to write the code on paper)
- Stack implementation from scratch using an array. Implement all the functions like push, pop, top, size, etc.
- Which sorting algorithms do you know? Which is better? I mentioned all the sorting algorithms then he told me to compare quick sort and merge sort and also mention the time complexities of both. Finally he told me to code the Merge Sort Algorithm.
- We had only 4 minutes left, then he told me to complete the Reverse string function using recursion in 4 minutes.
Note:
Here the interviewer was very strict with making changes in the code after writing, He said that “These are the golden lines of code you have written, it should execute now if we write on the compiler.” We can’t make any changes at the stage of dry running. I was able to dry run all my codes of these 3 questions and he was satisfied with it.
3. At the end, he asked me if I had any questions, I asked 2-3 questions and the interview was over. (Be prepared with your questions beforehand only, you must ask 2-3 questions in order to show interest towards the company.)
6 students were eliminated after this round, so around 19 were shortlisted for the second round.

Technical Round 2 (45 mins) (17th August 2023)
1. This round too started with the famous “Tell me about yourself?”
2. Then he asked which language do you prefer and why? I replied C++, then he asked me difference between C++ and java.
3. Then he started asking questions about Oops. He asked me to explain the principles of OOPS, and I asked a clarifying question whether the question means Pillars of OOPS.
4. Then he asked in detail about inheritance. He asked why we use inheritance, I answered reusability, then we asked is it only reusability or any other benefits as well? I gave him 2-3 points and he was satisfied.
5. Then he asked me are you familiar with SQL? I said yes, then he started asking me complex queries which included all the aggregate functions, joins, sub query, correlated query, having clause etc. I was able to answer all his questions so he seems to be satisfied.
6. But then he asked me how will you handle Null and Not Null values. I answered his question by using where condition and with statements like IS NULL and IS NOT NULL, but he wanted the NULL values as well which should be replaced by some string. At this point i was not sure about the answer, so i said No.
7. So he said, are you aware of the Oracle functions like nvl? Then he told me the syntax of nvl and told me to complete the above query and complete his requirement. I was able to do so and he seemed to be satisfied.
8. Now he was an expert on MongoDB and I mentioned MongoDB as one of the skills in my resume, he started asking a lot of questions on MongoDB, many of which I was not aware of.
9. I told him honestly that I am not comfortable with all the Mongo queries and I have just worked with some of the basic functionalities and authentication parts.
10. Then he asked me if i have any questions, i asked 2-3 and the interview was ended.
After the Technical Round 2, immediately I was called for the HR Round. Infact, I was the first one who was called for the HR Round. The students were called on the rolling basis, and 4 students were not called for the HR Interview so they were eliminated after the 2nd Round.

Hiring Manager Round (25 mins) (17th August 2023)
1. The interviewer was very friendly and he made me comfortable by asking questions like how was your day, how are you feeling, and how much you enjoyed the process.
2. In the HR Round, he asked me why do you want to join BNY Mellon?
3. He also looked at my resume, he asked me related to some of the projects and we had a detailed discussion
4. Since we both worked on Machine learning and generative models we had a great point of interest and I tried to link all of my skills with the BNY Mellon’s requirements.
5. He asked me how would you bridge the gap between academics and work in industries?
6. What are your strengths and weaknesses
7. Where do you see yourself in the next 3-5 years?
8. Lastly, the interviewer asked If I had any questions.
I was certainly sure that the HR Round was really a great discussion and I have a strong chance of selection.
On that same day, at 9:55 PM, the results were released. 12 students were chosen, and I was one of them😊.
All the best everyone and just believe in yourself!
You will get the company which you deserve and is relevant with your skills and expectations. Keep working Hard!
